notes:
Summary: SlateBridge builds an IDE-centric copilot embedded in their web and desktop editors. Primary ask = ultra-low TTFT for token streaming + predictable token budgets so devs don't see bursts or runaway completions. Wants model/version pinning so product team can roll forward/back without breaking local UX.

Highlights from discovery call: 
- "In-editor suggestions must appear instantly — users notice >50ms lag" (product lead).
- Prefers streaming partial tokens to fill the editor as characters arrive; cannot afford big jitter spikes.
- Willing to run Dedicated pools for EU traffic; interested in VPC/private for IP-sensitive repos.
- Strong desire for automatic backpressure: when the editor is overloaded, server should either pause streaming, trim suggestions, or fallback to a smaller model low-latency stub.
- Token-budget policy: per-session soft cap (1k-2k) with graceful truncation and per-repo overrides. Need audit logs for quota usage and retention controls for snippets.

What we demoed: low-latency streaming, model pinning, rollout canary, prefix caching. Client asked for a jitter heatmap and TTFT percentiles (p50/p95/p99) in Console.

Quote to capture: "If the first token isn't effectively instant, engineers think the assistant is broken."

Stubs/links: security FAQ on Drive, pricing deck attached, Fireflies notes for meeting on 2026-02-24.

Short-term asks: POC config with 3 model flavors (opt-high-latency, opt-med, opt-low); streaming chunk size experiments; token-budget enforcement hooks to editor (cancel or pause signal).
